newsitem.title: UK: CAP failure likely, Europe agriculture must change.
newsitem.headline: CAP failure likely, Europe agriculture must change.

text.p: The European Union Common Agricultural Policy risked ending in failure like commodity pacts of the past, Clive Furness, director of commodity products at the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE), said on Thursday.

Ultimately, CAP was like other market intervention measures, which were not supportable, and would will fail like the tin support pacts and the international coffee agreement, Furness said at the International Derivatives Conference.
The reasons behind the CAP were worthy, but while the world had moved on it had not.
"What is needed is to bring European agriculture into the modern world...what is needed is to put money into risk management," Furness said.
This was essential, or Europe's agriculture markets would suffer the same fate as coffee, tin, and other commodities in the past.
"Europe has the chance to remove artificially supported markets - when the CAP collapses it will be too late," he said.
Furness said the industry needed to explore areas such as futures and forward markets, as well as the over-the-counter (OTC) sector.
He said that LIFFE was prepared therefore to work with the European Union (EU) and the farm commissioners to a develop the necessary training and education programme.
